newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Deve Gowda named caretaker premier.
newsitem.headline: India's Deve Gowda named caretaker premier.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda said on Saturday that he had tendered his resignation to President Shankar Dayal Sharma and been asked to remain as caretaker prime minister.

"The president has accepted my resignation and asked me to continue as caretaker prime minister until alternative arrangements are made," Deve Gowda, who had earlier lost a confidence vote in parliament, told reporters as he left the presidential palace.
Earlier, Deve Gowda had said he would not recommend dissolution of the lower house of parliament. If the lower house, the Lok Sabha, is dissolved, general elections must be held.

Both Deve Gowda's United Front coalition and the Congress party, which triggered his downfall by withdrawing its vital backing, have said they would prefer to avert mid-term elections as they could strengthen the Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
The United Front and Congress held informal talks on Friday to try to strike a deal that would lead to a new government and sidestep polls.
The two formations were expected to hold meetings later on Saturday to determine their strategies.
